newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag sees small 1996 operating profits gain.
newsitem.headline: Viag sees small 1996 operating profits gain.

text.p: German mixed industrial Viag AG confirmed on Thursday that it expected operating profit in full-year 1996 to be "a little better" than in 1995.
Speaking to journalists in Frankfurt, Viag's management board chairman Georg Obermeier said: "We expect the operating profit to be a little better than in 1995."

Viag said at its interim results in August that operating profits grew 10 percent in the first half of 1996, although a raft of one-off charges brought pre-tax profit down 21 percent to 1.178 billion marks for the period.
Obermeier said operating profits at its core energy division would be better in the current year, but that operating profits at its computer wholesale unit Computer 2000 would be weaker.
Operating profits in its chemical sector, dominated by its SKW Trostberg subsidiary, would now be worse than in 1995.
Viag's packaging business would see improvements on the previous year, while its logistics sector would be "a little better" than in 1995.
Obermeier said he was confident its consortium would win the fourth German mobile telephone licence, due to be awarded next year, as no other candidates had yet applied for the licence.
The consortium also includes RWE AG and British Telecom.

"If we don't get the licence, then we have a problem and the strategy we've been following up until now will be redundant. I am optimistic that we have a good chance of winning the licence," said Obermeier.
